transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh it's Jordan from Redwood. We'll kick off, quick agenda — benchmark recap, tuning we did, and next steps. Priya from the SE team is with me.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Hi all, thanks. Hi Sam, Maya, Daniel. I'll start with the numbers and then we can dig in.
[00:20] Sam Carter: Thanks. We skimmed the summary you sent, excited to see the detail.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Cool. So baseline for reference is the provider you were using, BaselineCloud, with their default endpoint. Our running POC used the same model family (open-llm-7b-ish variant) but with Redwood optimizations: int8 quantization, workload-aware batching, and prefix KV caching.
[00:40] Priya Nair: Key numbers: mean p50 latency under load was ~110 ms on our 8xA100 equivalent pool, p95 420 ms. BaselineCloud numbers we measured in the same harness: p50 ~240 ms, p95 ~810 ms. Throughput at 99% quality envelope: Redwood delivered ~180 RPS vs BaselineCloud ~90 RPS for this model and request profile.
[01:05] Maya Lopez: Sorry quick question — are those numbers with streaming enabled or full response? We send fairly long responses sometimes so curious.
[01:11] Priya Nair: Good call — these were end-to-end token generation times with streaming disabled so full-response times. With streaming on, tail latency improves for most interactive flows. There is some variation with sequence length; we ran 128/512/1024 token distributions.
[01:26] Daniel Kim: How reproducible were these? Our baseline tests had a lot of variance depending on batch sizes.
[01:31] Priya Nair: We saw variance but we controlled for batch size in the harness. We tested with three batch configs: small (1-4), medium (8-16), and large (32+). The biggest delta vs the baseline came from continuous batching behavior and the KV cache: our runtime maintains per-conversation cached KV so repeated prefixes almost zeroed out recompute.
[01:50] Speaker 2: There was also some kernel selection improvements, we selected fused attention kernels for that specific arch — that helped p95.
[01:58] Jordan Lee: On the tuning side, top things we flipped were: int8 quantization which saved memory and allowed denser packing (thus higher effective concurrency), aggressive prefix KV caching for chat sessions, and dynamic kernel selection which lowers tail latency.
[02:15] Sam Carter: Any quality hits from int8? We can't have hallucination rate go up a lot.
[02:19] Priya Nair: We ran an eval on your eval set (the 800 prompts you shared) — delta in top-1 quality metrics was negligible (<1.5% on our automatic metrics). We did see a couple edge cases with rare tokens where int8 slightly changed logits; we flagged those and rolled a micro calibration step.
[02:36] Maya Lopez: That matches our internal expectation. We'll need to run human evals but good to see the automatic numbers.
[02:42] Jordan Lee: We also compared cost-per-inference: because of higher throughput and packing efficiency, Redwood's cost-per-req in this config was ~45% lower than the BaselineCloud bill-for-equivalent-performance. That's after factoring in cluster utilization and kernel-level improvements.
[02:58] Daniel Kim: The numbers sound promising. What about security/compliance? We need SOC2, SAML, and KMS for key management.
[03:06] Alex Gomez: From CSM side — we've shared the SOC2 report in the security folder earlier; we can also walk you through SAML SSO and KMS integration steps. For Private/Dedicated options, you can bring your own KMS or we can integrate with your cloud KMS.
[03:22] Priya Nair: Note that for Dedicated pilots we can do a VPC peering or private link; also on-prem package is an option if egress policy is an issue.
[03:31] Sam Carter: For the pilot timeline: we want to run a 24h production-like test. Can Redwood initiate that and share logs/metrics?
[03:38] Priya Nair: Yes — our plan is to run the 24h single-tenant harness with the same request distribution and quantization config. We'll capture p50/p90/p95/time-series, kernel perf counters, and GPU utilization. We'll also produce a comparison sheet mapping every test case to BaselineCloud number.
[03:53] Jordan Lee: I'll share the spreadsheet and test harness repo. That contains the command lines we used and the infrastructure config.
[03:58] Maya Lopez: One more clarif — tokenization differences sometimes skewed counts in your spreadsheet vs ours, where you reported lower token counts. Can we sync tokenizers?
[04:06] Priya Nair: Absolutely — we used the model's default tokenizer in the harness but we'll run a tokenizer parity check. Maya, if you can send a sample of 10k requests we can align on exact token counts.
[04:15] Maya Lopez: Will do.
[04:16] Daniel Kim: Networking note — we'll need a static egress IP list for our firewall team, also a specific CIDR for VPC peering.
[04:24] Jordan Lee: We'll provide ip ranges and a short network doc.
[04:27] Priya Nair: Quick note on experimental results: for long context (1k tokens), we saw a slightly smaller gap vs baseline on p95 (Redwood p95 ~720 ms vs Baseline ~900 ms) — so gap narrows as context increases, likely due to kv cache hit rates and kernel saturation.
[04:45] Sam Carter: Interesting — any configs to further reduce p95 for long context?
[04:49] Priya Nair: A couple approaches: 1) hybrid batching: cap batch sizes during spikes, 2) early token streaming to reduce perceived latency, 3) splitting long prompts into prefix + user tokens to maximize KV reuse. We'll propose exact settings in the spreadsheet.
[05:05] Jordan Lee: Ok let's capture action items. Jordan to send benchmark spreadsheet and pricing for Dedicated pilot. Priya to run 24h load test starting Wed 2026-05-20 and share raw logs. Maya to give sample request set. Daniel to confirm network allowlist.
[05:20] Priya Singh (PM): Can you also include the SAML metadata and a sample KMS integration doc? We need that to share with infra.
[05:27] Alex Gomez: Yes, will include SOC2, SAML guide and KMS notes in the packet.
[05:32] Speaker 3: Slight transcription note, there was a moment where the harness overloaded one host — we caught it and adjusted concurrency, that explains the spike in the 03:00 hour.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: Thanks. Any other blockers from FinOptima?
[05:43] Sam Carter: No blockers, team just wants to validate the 24h run and finalize pricing for the Dedicated pilot.
[05:50] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll target follow-up 2026-05-26 10:00 PT to review results. I'll send calendar invite.
[05:57] Maya Lopez: Thanks everyone.
[05:59] Priya Nair: Thanks, bye.
[06:02] End of call: 45 minutes recorded. Note: some speaker labels were auto-assigned and may be slightly off in places, minor transcription errors present (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, and a couple proper nouns).
